projects.name: Co-production, implementation and on Action / impact-based forecasting in Lesotho
projects.description:
OBJECTIVE: Strengthening the transition to people-centred, action-based warnings, formalising coordination and roles, embedding GEDSI considerations, and establishing learning processes that enhance the effectiveness and usability of forecasting and warning services in Lesotho.

TIMEFRAME: February 2026 to March 2027

Contributing Partners: FCDO through UK Met Office: 80 000 USD, WMO: 25 000 USD and SAWS: 15 000 USD.

Sub Activities

Sub Activity 1: Identify and prioritise user needs for Action-Based Forecasting by engaging at least four key user groups (disaster management, agriculture, health, and local government) for each priority hazard.

Sub Activity 2: Co-produce and validate impact tables and risk matrices for Heavy Rainfall and Cold Waves, endorsed by LMS, DMA, and relevant line departments.

Sub Activity 3: Strengthen coordination and clarify institutional roles by jointly developing draft inter-agency Standard Operating Procedures (SOPs) that define responsibilities, decision thresholds, and response actions.

Sub Activity 4: Improve communication and accessibility of warnings by testing at least three dissemination channels (e.g. radio, mobile messaging, community networks) and incorporating GEDSI-responsive communication approaches.

Sub Activity 5: Advance implementation of Action-Based Forecasts and Warnings by conducting at least one validation or simulation exercise per hazard to test usability and trigger early action.

Sub Activity 6: Generate learning to inform future scale-up, with documented lessons and recommendations feeding into a national Action-Based Forecasting roadmap.

Required Budget: USD 1 million, Available: USD 120 000.00

projects.name: UNESCO_Africa-Europe Partnerships for Culture: Promoting Culture and Heritage-based Sustainable Tourism in Southern Africa
projects.description:
The project “Africa-Europe Partnerships for Culture: Promoting Culture and Heritage-based Sustainable Tourism in Southern Africa”, a European Union project implemented by UNESCO, will contribute to strengthening the contribution of culture and heritage to sustainable development, notably through enhancing culture and heritage-based tourism development, diversifying tourism products and delivering high-quality visitor experiences at selected UNESCO-designated sites and cities. These activities aim to contribute to improving livelihoods of the communities in the region, including youth, women and indigenous peoples, through capacity building and the creation of opportunities for income-generation and jobs.

Through innovative partnerships, the project will invest in the development of engaging storytelling, the production of meaningful digital content and authentic, relevant products incorporating new narratives. It will enhance cultural production capacities to develop community-based programming and tourism offers at the participating UNESCO-designated sites and cities. At the same time, the project presents a unique occasion to promote international cooperation and peer-to-peer learning opportunities among the six target Southern African countries, namely Botswana, Eswatini, Lesotho, Namibia, South Africa and Zimbabwe, as well as with European Union countries, to foster regional integration and social cohesion.
